title: SRSSF: Stability-Reliability Spectral-Spatial Fusion for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral Image Classification is an importanttopic in remote sensing with numerous applications in precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, defence, and more. It helps classify material composition by mapping spectral signatures from each pixel. Despite its potential, it faces persistent challenges due to the scarcity of labelled data and high dimensionality. This makes it difficult to achieve robust performance that can generalize well. To address this problem, we propose SRSSF (Stability-Reliability Spectral-Spatial Fusion), a hybrid mixture-of-experts framework for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. It fuses a compact, stability-selected spectral representation with full-spectrum spatial and joint spectral-spatial descriptors (extended morphological, attribute-like, and Gabor texture profiles), combined through validation-derived reliability weights rather than fixed or heuristic fusion rules. SRSSF is evaluated under a strict, footprint-level spatially disjoint protocol in which entire patch receptive fields are guaranteed non-overlapping across training, validation, and test partitions, not mere center pixels. It has an automated, geometry-only (label- and accuracy-independent) seed-acceptance procedure and requires a minimum dataset-specific test-set size for training. The framework is benchmarked against fourteen classical and CNN spectral/spatial baselines and a dedicated ablation suite, across four benchmark datasets (Indian Pines, Pavia University, Salinas, and the Kennedy Space Center (KSC)). Our framework achieves the best OA, AA, and κ on every dataset, with OA scores of 56.43,91.94,90.50, and 75.96 at Indian-Pines, Pavia University, Salinas, and KSC, respectively.
